visible_text: 設定画面を開けませんでした

observation.happening: Error notification banner indicating a settings screen failed to open. Contains warning triangle icon, Japanese error message, blue retry action button, close button, and unexplained levels/volume icon on right in circle.
observation.most_important: Recovery action is prominent and clear (もう一度開く)
observation.next_action: User can retry opening settings or dismiss the notification
anomalies: Levels/volume icon on right doesn't semantically match error context—creates visual confusion about message intent
Mixed icon semantics: warning triangle + levels icon

ai_look: Icon choice feels arbitrary rather than semantically motivated

visible_text: 質問したときだけ Claude に送信

observation.happening: Dark-themed informational toast announcing screenshot capability with explanation. Minimal design: file icon, clear label, supporting text, close button. No action buttons—purely informational.
observation.most_important: Transparent communication of data handling (only sends when asked)
observation.next_action: User dismisses notification or lets it fade

3680.why: Exemplary minimal notification. Zero wasted space, dark neutral tone, informative hierarchy, calm presentation. Text reads naturally (not over-explained). Appropriate icon. Only lacks distinctiveness but that's acceptable for system notifications.

observation.happening: Error/warning banner for missing Astra configuration. Contains explanatory instruction text in two lines, blue action button to open system settings, close button, and levels icon in purple circle on right.
observation.most_important: User must manually enable Astra in system settings
observation.next_action: Click 'システム設定を開く' to resolve
anomalies: Levels icon repeats across error messages without clear semantic connection
Purple tint on circle suggests warning/system level but mixed messaging with two-line instruction

ai_look: Levels icon reuse across unrelated error types feels systematic but unexplained

visible_text: AstraDbg を再起動すると使えます

observation.happening: Settings panel showing three service toggles (AnyDesk, AstraDbg, ChatGPT), all currently ON (blue switches). AstraDbg row includes secondary text explaining restart needed. Red numbered badge '1' on far left.
observation.most_important: Services are configurable via toggles; AstraDbg requires restart to take effect
observation.next_action: User can toggle services on/off; must restart AstraDbg for changes
anomalies: Red '1' badge on left edge serves unclear purpose—notification count? Warning? Not explained visually.
Badge creates asymmetric visual weight on left side

ai_look: Unexplained badge feels like leftover notification indicator or design system artifact
3E91.why: Toggle states are clear and switches work visually, but the red badge creates visual tension without communicating its purpose. The 'restart required' state for AstraDbg is handled well with secondary text, but badge integration feels incomplete.

observation.most_important: Screen recording permission required; user must enable in system settings
observation.next_action: Click 'システム設定を開く' to grant permission

Icon doesn't relate to screen recording semantically

ai_look: Repeated levels icon across all error types creates unresolved design language question

visible_text: 画面収録を設定できました

observation.happening: Success notification banner with green checkmark confirming '画面収録を設定できました' (screen recording successfully configured). Minimal design: checkmark, text, close button, and levels icon in teal circle on right.
observation.next_action: User dismisses notification or waits for auto-fade
anomalies: Levels icon appears now in success context with teal color—confirms icon is used across all message types (error/warning/success) without semantic consistency

AF8F.why: Exemplary success notification. Single clear message, green checkmark instantly communicates success, teal circle is calming and positive. Minimal density, perfect geometry, zero visual noise. The levels icon here works because success state is unambiguous. Only limitation is lack of distinctiveness, but appropriate for system notifications.
